title: Streaming fanout load probe & p95 regression detector for SSE/WebSocket chat
creator: Asha Patil
description:
Problem: We have intermittent p95 latency regressions and token/sec throughput drops for streaming chat endpoints (SSE and WebSocket) under multi-tenant fanout patterns. Existing synthetic load drivers focus on non-streaming request/response shapes and do not model long-lived connections or KV-cache warmups.

Goal: Build a repeatable, observable load probe that exercises streaming chat/completions at realistic concurrency and fanout (multiple downstream model shards per request), captures per-connection p95 and tokens/sec, detects regressions automatically, and integrates with our perf dashboards and CI gating.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reliable capture of tokens/sec and per-connection p95 for SSE and WebSocket streams at target scale (up to 25k concurrent streams in dedicated test infra).
- Regression detector that emits an alert when p95 increases by >20% vs baseline across three consecutive runs or tokens/sec drops by >15%.
- Dashboard with sample-level histogram, service-side and client-side p95, token emission rates, and tail latencies for handling KV cache misses vs warmed runs.
- CI integration: an optional gating job that runs lightweight fanout probe and fails when regression detector is tripped.

Scope:
- Implement a new Go load probe (stream-fanout-probe) that manages long-lived SSE and WebSocket connections, simulates user streaming patterns, supports configurable fanout across model variants, and outputs structured logs compatible with our perf ingestion pipeline.
- Instrument metrics: client-side stream p50/p95/p99, server-observed per-token latency, tokens/sec, connection churn, error codes, and KV cache hit/miss tags.
- Add a regression detection component (Python) that compares runs against golden baselines stored in S3 and produces human-readable evidence and CI-friendly exit codes.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full-fidelity multi-region chaos or full tenant replication; those will be follow-ups.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Language: Go for the load driver for low GC jitter with runtime's native HTTP/WS clients; Python for the regression analysis to reuse existing statistical libs and integration with our alerting pipeline.
- Determinism vs realism: We will support deterministic replay of prompts for regressions but enable randomized jittered prompt mixes for exploratory runs to uncover edge cases.
- Metrics granularity: Collect per-connection stream-level histograms (cost in storage) but roll up to aggregated histograms per-run for long-term storage.

Instrumentation details:
- Client emits structured JSON events to stdout; a small Fluent Bit config in test infra forwards to perf-ingest (kinesis-like).
- Each token emission event: {run_id, connection_id, seq, token_ts, server_received_ts, server_sent_ts, token_length, model_variant, kv_cache_hit}. We will flatten these into CSV-like lines when sending to S3 to keep ingestion costs predictable.

Test scenarios and ramp profiles:
1) Warmup profile: 5k connections, 1k concurrent token-emitting streams; KV cache warmup enabled. Run 20 minutes.
2) Cold start profile: 5k connections, KV cache cold; measure server-side p95 for first 5k tokens.
3) Fanout spike: Single logical request fanout to 4 model shards, measure aggregation and worst-case p95.
4) Churn test: 10k connects/disconnects per minute while maintaining 2k steady streams to stress routing and connection bookkeeping.
5) CI-light probe: ~200 connections, short (5m) run to detect gross regressions quickly.

Regression detection rules:
- Baseline computed as median of last 5 non-failing baseline runs for each profile.
- Trigger if run.p95 > baseline.p95 * 1.20 and p95 percentile shift is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney U, p < 0.01), or tokens/sec < baseline.tokens/sec * 0.85.
- Require detection on at least two of three successive runs or across two different profiles before opening a high-severity alert.

Alerting & dashboards:
- Add Grafana dashboard panel templates: stream p95 heatmap, tokens/sec over time, per-model-variant delta vs baseline, connection churn heatmap.
- Regression detector posts detailed triage artifact to #perf-alerts Slack channel with a link to an evidence page (S3 HTML + trace links) and a suggested owner.

Deliverables:
- stream-fanout-probe (Go) + build and Dockerfile.
- regression-detector (Python) CLI and CI job wrapper.
- Perf dashboard templates and a Confluence runbook for interpreting detector output.
- Example baseline datasets for warm and cold profiles in S3.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype in staging infra (ENG-21901-pt1) and run manually against runtime-staging.
2) Validate metrics ingestion and dashboard (ENG-21901-pt2).
3) Wire regression-detector to nightly perf pipeline as optional job (ENG-21901-pt3).
4) Promote CI-light probe into mainline PR checks for runtime-1.22 if stable.

comments: 2026-01-30 — Daniel Kim: Spiked a small prototype driver to validate connection handling. Observed large variance in reported token timestamps due to server batching; added server_sent_ts tagging requirement to the metrics contract.

2026-02-05 — Maria Gomez (perf): Ran warmup profile in staging; tokens/sec matched expectations but p95 had bimodal distribution — likely KV cache misses during initial fanout. We should separate warm and cold baselines.
2026-02-18 — Asha Patil: Chose Go for driver after testing Node and Go prototypes under 5k connections. Go had lower jitter on token emission. Created initial GH skeleton at infra/pull/4321.
2026-02-25 — Security review (Liam Chen): No secrets persisted by the probe; verify that S3 baselines are encrypted by default. Marked security_review_required=false for now.
2026-03-03 — Daniel Kim: Implemented regression-detector MVP. It compares CSV aggregates and emits JUnit-style output for CI. Hooked into nightly perf job (manual run).

2026-03-09 — Engineering review (Tech Leads): Feedback: make per-connection histograms optional via --histogram flag to reduce ingestion cost; add option to simulate variable token rates per user class. Added to scope and estimate increased by 2 points.
2026-03-10 — Daniel Kim: Added CI-light job config at .circleci/config.yml -> job: stream-fanout-smoke. Next: add Grafana panels and wire detector alerts to #perf-alerts.
